notable_absence.finding: Step 10 ('(Optional) To add an additional layout, repeat the previous steps') is the same repeatable one-to-many pattern already flagged as unmodelable in this batch's other pages (exception tokenizer's exception patterns) - a single date/time parser can have multiple layout entries, and the registry has no predicate for that cardinality.

cross_component_finding: This page is the batch's clearest NEGATIVE case for analyzer composition: unlike create-custom-character-filter.json, create-custom-tokenizer.json and create-custom-token-filter.json - each of which states in its own Next Steps sentence that the component 'can [be used] with a custom analyzer' - this page's Next Steps instead says the custom date/time parser can be 'set ... as the default date/time parser for your Search index' (an index-level default, via set-advanced-settings.md#date-time), and 'Create a Custom Analyzer' appears only as an ordinary sibling bullet in the generic 'continue customizing' list, not as a stated usage relation. This matches the concurrent batch's own modeling choice (search:full-text-index -hasInternalComponent-> search:date-time-parser, not search:custom-analyzer -hasInternalComponent-> search:date-time-parser) and confirms the dispatch brief's caveat was correctly narrow: the tokenizer/character-filter/token-filter composition is specific to the analyzer, and date/time parsers (like the default analyzer setting itself) are a separate, index-level customization living alongside analyzers under 'Customize Index', not inside one.
